title: Understanding Singular Value Decomposition
text: When performing Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on a matrix, the matrix is decomposed into three other matrices: U, S, and $$V^T$$. Each of these matrices has specific properties. Can you recall what these properties are and how they relate to the original matrix X?

title: Properties of the S Matrix
text: The S matrix in the SVD decomposition contains the singular values of the original matrix X. These singular values are always arranged in a specific order. Do you remember what this order is and why it might be important?

title: Order of Singular Values
text: How are the singular values in the S matrix arranged?
